text.text: (1) No. Formal status and insurance rules apply. (2) No. The automatic deadline ban continues until inspection is carried out. Only the applicable restricted inspection/repair trip is permitted; vehicle status, insurance, tax and safety conditions must be satisfied. Follow the inspection result and check for any further prohibition before ordinary use.
Build an ownership checklist for registration, insurance, inspection and vehicle status.

The registered owner of an on-road car must have compulsory motor insurance. Not using the car, or having a defect or driving prohibition, does not by itself end that obligation; formal off-road status matters. Compulsory insurance covers specified traffic injuries and damage to others, not every loss to your own car. Optional cover varies by policy.

For an ordinary car or light goods vehicle up to 3,500 kg, the normal inspection sequence is: first by 36 months after the month of first use, second by 24 months after the first inspection month, then by 14 months after the preceding inspection month. Check the recorded date and any special category or exemption for your vehicle. An earlier inspection changes the next calculation; an old reminder is not proof of the current deadline.

An on-road registration status, valid insurance and completed inspection answer different questions. Check the vehicle's status and any prohibition before use, and deal with tax obligations through the current official service. A car being physically driveable does not establish legal readiness.

Transportstyrelsen currently provides eligible private-person transfers through Mina sidor; other cases may require the latest registration certificate part 2. The service has eligibility conditions. Consult the current instructions instead of relying on an old app or a remembered screen sequence. Part 1 and the vehicle enquiry service provide technical information; protect ownership documents appropriately.
Resolve a missed inspection
If the required periodic inspection deadline is missed, an automatic driving ban (

) applies. You remain responsible even without a reminder. Booking a later appointment does not end the ban. The deadline ban lasts until the inspection has been carried out; follow its result, since defects can bring a new prohibition or a repair/reinspection requirement. Check the vehicle record before ordinary use.
With an overdue-inspection ban and on-road status (
), only the shortest suitable route to a repair workshop for repair or to an inspection business for inspection is permitted. If the vehicle is off-road (

) and the ban still applies, the exception is the shortest suitable route to the nearest inspection business. Traffic insurance and other applicable requirements still matter; the off-road exception requires no unpaid vehicle taxes. It does not permit errands or commuting. A prohibition issued because the vehicle is dangerously defective has different conditions: it must be recovered from the place where that prohibition is issued.

An ordinary light car's recorded inspection deadline is 31 October 2026. Without the required inspection, the deadline ban starts on 1 November. An appointment on 5 November does not allow normal driving on 2 November. Arrange a permitted inspection trip, or transport if it cannot be driven safely and lawfully, then follow the inspection result. These dates illustrate the rule; use the actual vehicle's record.

A buyer collects an on-road car but assumes the seller's insurance is enough for the trip home. The buyer checks the transfer and arranges the required cover from the applicable ownership date before driving. The sale does not transfer the seller's insurance as personal cover for the buyer.
Check your understanding
(1) Does garaging an on-road car automatically end compulsory insurance? (2) The inspection deadline passed, but you booked an appointment. May you commute meanwhile?
Keep a record of dates and obligations, then verify them against the current vehicle record.

objectives.text: Build an ownership checklist for registration, insurance, inspection and vehicle status.

text.text: No. It operates within the friction available, and stopping still depends on speed, surface, tyres and conditions.
Explain why safety systems and powertrain differences do not remove your duties to observe and control.

Trafikverket describes modern protection as including crashworthiness and systems such as lane assistance and automatic emergency braking. These functions can help, but a good safety rating is not a promise that any collision can be avoided. Recent official crash testing also shows the limits of automatic braking in severe truck-trailer collision scenarios.

ABS is anti-lock braking. It helps retain the ability to develop steering and braking forces together, within available friction. Stability control reduces the risk of skid crashes; it does not create extra road grip or excuse excessive speed. The driver still has to maintain control and an appropriate speed.
A plug-in hybrid can operate on electricity and with a combustion engine. That difference matters when interpreting fuel use and emissions: do not assume that every journey is electrically powered.

For the actual vehicle, establish how it becomes ready to move, how drive and reverse are selected, how it is secured, and what warnings or assistance limitations need attention. Do not transfer a universal gear-change, engine-speed, coasting or brake-check recipe between manual, automatic, hybrid and electric vehicles. Vehicle-specific procedures need the vehicle's own instructions and practical teaching. The curriculum's role is to help you identify those questions, not guess their answers.
Assistance has limits

In this chapter
· Look beyond the exhaust
· Use energy with foresight
· Choose the journey as well as the car
· Check where the vehicle can go

It is not an official source and cannot replace official information from Trafikverket and Transportstyrelsen. Always consult their current guidance and the applicable rules.

documents.title: Reduce the impact of each journey

text.text: (1) Long-stored carbon becomes CO₂, strengthening the greenhouse effect. A catalyst converts other pollutants and works poorly just after a cold start. (2) CO impairs blood oxygen transport; NOx irritates airways and contributes to acidification and ground-level ozone; particles harm airways. (3) No: production and electricity supply still matter. A plug-in hybrid can charge externally; a non-plug-in hybrid cannot. (4) Choose a purpose-built wash collecting and treating wastewater.
Compare climate, air-quality and noise effects without assuming that a vehicle has no environmental impact.

Transportstyrelsen distinguishes several effects. Greenhouse-gas emissions relate to the amount of travel, fuels, energy efficiency and electrification. Air pollution includes exhaust emissions and wear particles from brakes, tyres and the road. Noise is another effect, with tyre-road noise becoming important as speed rises. These are different measures: improving one does not prove that every environmental effect has disappeared.

Ask what a comparison includes. Does an emissions figure describe a test result, the actual journey or a broader lifecycle? Are you comparing equal distances and occupancy? If the basis is missing, avoid a confident numerical conclusion. This lesson does not assign a universal emissions saving to a powertrain or declare a whole journey “zero impact.”

A plug-in hybrid combines electrical and combustion-engine operation. Transportstyrelsen changed the weighting used for new registrations in 2026 to better reflect the mix of those modes. The general lesson is to understand what a reported figure represents; it is not a promise about your next journey's consumption.
Understand emissions

children.text: Emissions explained · Fossil carbon and a cold catalyst.

text.text: Fossil petrol contains carbon stored for millions of years. Burning it combines that carbon with oxygen and releases CO₂ into the atmosphere. The added CO₂ strengthens the natural greenhouse effect and contributes to warming.

A conventional petrol car's three-way catalyst reduces carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides by chemical conversion. It needs sufficient heat to become effective, so it is least effective just after a cold start. Conversion products include water and CO₂: cleaning up these pollutants does not capture the fossil carbon or cancel its climate impact. No single warm-up time applies to every car.
Keep CO distinct from CO₂. The table summarises different mechanisms; one cleaner exhaust measure cannot stand for all of them.

cells.text: CO₂ · carbon dioxide
Added fossil CO₂ strengthens the greenhouse effect.
CO · carbon monoxide
Binds strongly to haemoglobin and interferes with the blood's oxygen transport.
NOx · nitrogen oxides
Can irritate airways, contribute to acidification and, with hydrocarbons and sunlight, form ground-level ozone.
Traffic particles
Exhaust and wear particles can enter and harm the respiratory system.

label.text: Trafikverket: CO, NOx and particle mechanisms

text.text: Compare powertrains and washing

children.text: Powertrain and washing · Check the boundary.

text.text: A battery-electric car uses only electricity for propulsion and has no combustion tailpipe exhaust while driving. That does not remove impacts from vehicle/battery production, raw-material extraction or electricity supply. Tyre and road wear still matter. A plug-in hybrid combines electric and combustion operation and its traction battery can be charged externally. A conventional non-plug-in hybrid cannot be charged from an external electricity supply.

label.text: Trafikverket: electric cars and hybrid types

text.text: Choose a purpose-built automatic or self-service wash that collects and treats its wastewater. Washing on an ordinary street or driveway can carry oil, metals and cleaning chemicals into ground or surface water. Treatment reduces the problem but does not remove every pollutant. Follow the facility's product instructions and local water-protection rules.

label.text: Göteborg environmental authority: washing and treatment

text.text: A catalyst-equipped petrol car still releases fossil CO₂. An electric car avoids combustion exhaust on that drive, but needs a broader production-and-energy comparison. For either car, choose washing by how the dirty water is handled, rather than assuming a mild detergent makes street runoff harmless.

Two vehicles are advertised using different environmental measures. One figure describes exhaust emissions under a test procedure; another describes noise. The learner does not rank them as though both figures measure the same thing. They first identify the question being answered and the information still missing.
Check your understanding

(1) Why does fossil petrol warm the climate, even with a catalyst, and when is that catalyst least effective? (2) Match CO, NOx and particles to their effects. (3) Does an electric car have no environmental impact; which hybrid can charge externally? (4) Where should washing water go?
Name the effect and the basis of comparison before making the claim.

objectives.text: Compare climate, air-quality and noise effects without assuming that a vehicle has no environmental impact.

text.text: (1) No. (2) Heat when needed, avoiding unnecessary runtime; retain comfort, alertness and clear windows without needless cooling. (3) Use a gear allowing smooth running without strain. Engine braking releases the accelerator with a suitable gear engaged; brake as needed. No universal RPM or zero-fuel promise. (4) Unload it before future trips; retain necessary equipment. (5) A: 80 × 6.5 ÷ 100 = 5.2 litres. B: 250 × 0.5 ÷ 100 = exactly 1.25 litres; ties-to-even to one decimal gives 1.2 litres. C: the rate difference is 7.5 − 6.2 = 1.3 litres/100 km; 200 × 1.3 ÷ 100 = 2.6 litres saved. These are supplied exercise rates, not guaranteed technique savings.
Plan anticipatory driving that reduces unnecessary energy use while preserving safety.

Transportstyrelsen recommends correct tyre pressure, observing speed limits and removing unused roof racks or roof boxes. Driving technique and environmental awareness are part of driver education and assessment.

Look ahead and respond early to a developing queue rather than accelerating towards it and then braking sharply. Choose a suitable speed and preserve a gap that lets you adapt smoothly. This is not an instruction to delay necessary braking: safe control and traffic duties come first. If you need to stop for a person, do so regardless of what an efficiency display suggests.

Prepare the vehicle for the trip. Check the specified tyre pressure and remove unnecessary external carrying equipment when it is no longer needed. Combine these habits with realistic route and timing decisions. Avoid claiming a fixed percentage saving: load, road, weather, vehicle and technique all affect the outcome.

Gear selection and deceleration strategies vary. Do not use a fixed engine-speed rule for every car or assume every powertrain cuts fuel or recovers energy in the same way. Learn the actual vehicle's approved operation with your instructor. This book does not recommend coasting in neutral or switching the vehicle off while moving.
Use energy with control

children.text: Practical energy choices · Prepare and control the car.

text.text: Use a timer with an installed electric engine heater so it warms the engine when needed, without running unnecessarily long. Set it for the intended departure using the equipment instructions and conditions; there is no universal heating duration.

label.text: Gagnef municipal energy advice: heater timer

text.text: Air conditioning consumes energy, but it can support comfort, alertness and clear windows. Avoid unnecessary cooling while keeping those safety benefits. Use the car's appropriate demisting controls; visibility takes priority over a saving. Cooling is not a remedy for sleep deprivation: stop and rest if drowsy. Revisit
for seeing clearly and
for attention.

label.text: NZ Transport Agency: cooling, alertness and demisting

text.text: In a conventional manual car, choose a suitably high gear in which the engine runs smoothly without labouring. Change down if the load or gradient makes that gear unsuitable. Engine braking means slowing with the accelerator released while a suitable gear remains engaged; do not disengage the drive by pressing the clutch or selecting neutral for this technique. Use the brakes whenever safety requires. Actual engine control varies, so this definition does not promise zero fuel use or a universal RPM.

label.text: Official vehicle agency: comfortable gear choice and in-gear deceleration

text.text: Unnecessary carried mass increases the demands on the vehicle. Unload heavy equipment you no longer need before future journeys, while retaining necessary safety and access equipment. Removing cargo is a different check from removing a roof box's air resistance.

label.text: Swedish public energy advice: minimise weight

text.text: Remove unused heavy equipment, schedule the heater for the trip, and keep effective demisting. On an uphill section, use the gear the car can comfortably handle; a high gear that strains the engine is not the intended economical technique.
Calculate journey consumption and savings

A consumption rate of 6.5 litres per 100 km means 6.5 litres for each 100 km under the supplied or measured conditions. A 200 km journey at the same assumed rate uses twice as much, while 50 km uses half as much. Actual consumption varies with vehicle, load, road, weather and driving.
supplies the driving context; the equations below are editorial arithmetic derived from the unit, not agency-prescribed formulas.

journey litres = distance in km × consumption in litres/100 km ÷ 100. Divide distance by 100 to find the number of 100 km portions, then multiply by the supplied rate. The kilometres cancel, leaving litres. Retain decimal working and round only the final result at the precision requested.

children.text: Consumption example · 120 km at 6.5 litres/100 km.

text.text: The journey contains 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2 portions of 100 km. Consumption = 1.2 × 6.5 =
. Do not multiply distance by the rate without dividing by 100; that would misread the unit.

litres saved = distance in km × reduction in litres/100 km ÷ 100. If two consumption rates are supplied, subtract the lower rate from the higher first. Multiply that difference by the number of 100 km portions. A supplied saving is an exercise assumption, not a guaranteed benefit of a particular driving technique.

children.text: Savings example · A reduction of 1.5 litres/100 km over 300 km.

text.text: The journey has 300 ÷ 100 = 3 portions. Savings = 3 × 1.5 =
. This is the difference in litres used, not the new total consumption. You need the original or new consumption rate to calculate either total.

children.text: Two-rate example · 7.0 and 6.5 litres/100 km over 240 km.

text.text: First find the rate difference: 7.0 − 6.5 = 0.5 litres/100 km. Savings = 240 × 0.5 ÷ 100 =
. The original journey uses 16.8 litres and the lower-rate journey 15.6 litres; their difference is also 1.2 litres. No percentage-saving promise is implied.
Exact values and displayed answers

children.text: Precision and midpoint rounding · Keep the exact result visible.

text.text: Some supplied savings exercises display one-decimal answers without specifying precision or a rounding convention in their prompts. Four such examples below use

for the displayed keyed value. This rounds to the nearest tenth; at an exact halfway value, choose the tenth whose retained digit is even. It differs from rounding a halfway value upwards. Do not call a rounded value the exact amount, or silently apply one convention where another is intended.

A reduction of 0.5 litres/100 km over 150 km gives exactly 0.75 litres, displayed as 0.8 to one decimal using ties-to-even. A reduction of 1.5 over 150 km gives exactly 2.25 litres, displayed as 2.2. A reduction of 0.5 over 250 km gives exactly 1.25 litres, displayed as 1.2. A reduction of 1.5 over 250 km gives exactly 3.75 litres, displayed as 3.8. The units for every reduction are litres/100 km.

With ordinary half-up rounding to one decimal, 2.25 becomes 2.3 and 1.25 becomes 1.3; ties-to-even gives 2.2 and 1.2. The exact products remain 2.25 and 1.25 litres. For these supplied examples, keep the exact arithmetic and the disclosed displayed-answer convention separate. For a new problem, follow its stated precision/convention; if they are absent, report the exact result and recognise that a rounded answer needs an assumption. Round once at the end, not the rate or intermediate product.

(A) Find journey consumption for 80 km at 6.5 litres/100 km. (B) Find the saving from a supplied reduction of 0.5 litres/100 km over 250 km, first exactly and then to one decimal using ties-to-even. (C) Find the saving over 200 km when supplied consumption falls from 7.5 to 6.2 litres/100 km. Give your units and show the rate difference where needed. Answers are in the separate lesson answer section.
Look ahead and preserve room

caption.text: The teal car approaches a queue on the right side of the road. Look ahead, retain room to stop and keep the crossing clear. The illustration does not specify a measured following distance.

text.text: You can see that a traffic queue is stationary ahead. You check behind and begin a controlled reduction in speed early, retaining enough room to stop. You do not accelerate simply to close the gap, and you do not roll into a crossing to preserve momentum.
Check your understanding

(1) May economy override a necessary stop? (2) How should you use an engine-heater timer and cooling? (3) What is a suitable high gear and engine braking in a manual car? (4) What should happen to unneeded heavy cargo? (5) Complete the three fuel-arithmetic exercises above, including exact and rounded values for B.
Reduce avoidable demands on the car while keeping full control of the journey.

objectives.text: Plan anticipatory driving that reduces unnecessary energy use while preserving safety.

text.text: No. Compare the actual needs, conditions and available options, then avoid unnecessary travel where practical.
Compare combining trips, walking, cycling, public transport and driving for a realistic personal journey.
The syllabus includes transport choices and the way personal circumstances influence them. A useful comparison recognises that people's access needs, schedules and available services differ.

Start with the purpose: reaching work, collecting goods, accompanying a person or making a visit. Then list workable options. Could two errands be combined? Could a nearby trip be walked or cycled safely? Is public transport available for both directions? If you share a car journey, can everyone use the required protection and travel without creating a rushed schedule?

Do not replace one unrealistic assumption with another. A route may be short but inaccessible to a particular person. A service may run outward but not at the return time. A car may solve those needs, while a different choice suits the following day's journey. The exercise is to make the choice deliberately.
Combine a practical journey

caption.text: Separate journeys: home - shop - home, then home - library - home. Combined journey: home - shop - library - home. These are schematic options, not measured routes or a promised saving. Check practical needs and timing.

text.text: A learner normally makes two separate drives to the same district. On a day when both appointments can be combined without leaving anyone waiting unsafely, the learner plans one return trip. No exact fuel saving is claimed; the decision avoids a duplicated journey.
Check your understanding
Is there one transport mode that is automatically best for every journey and every person?
Good planning includes asking whether to drive, not only how to drive.

text.text: (1) No. Check zone class, vehicle criteria, exemptions and current decision. (2) Studs wear roads and create airborne particles. Check the local decision, route, dates, exceptions and signs; national permitted season does not override a local ban.
Find official environmental-zone information and determine what to verify before entering.

Municipalities can introduce environmental zones under the national framework. Class 1 concerns heavy buses and heavy goods vehicles; class 2 concerns passenger cars and light buses/goods vehicles. For class 2, spark-ignition vehicles need Euro 5 or Euro 6 and diesel vehicles need Euro 6. For light vehicles, class 3 ordinarily permits only electric, fuel-cell or qualifying gas vehicles; gas vehicles must meet the specified Euro 6 emissions criteria. A light plug-in hybrid is not admitted merely because it can sometimes run electrically. Exemptions exist for specified vehicles and uses.
Recognise environmental-zone starts and ends Independent official examples. Match an ending to the same class at the start. These signs do not assert a current municipal boundary.
Continue the learning
Continue the learning
Continue the learning

Check three layers: the national vehicle criteria, the current local restriction and your actual vehicle record. A national possibility to introduce a zone does not mean every city has introduced it. A manufacturer's marketing name does not prove the vehicle's recorded emissions class. Locate the applicable decision and signs for the actual route.
Charging and parking are different A charging facility and a parking qualification are different. Neither symbol gives permission to enter an environmental zone.

Compare a breakdown on an ordinary road, a motorway and in a tunnel.

If a breakdown leaves a vehicle where stopping is prohibited, it must be moved to a suitable place as soon as possible, subject to the special rules for an accident scene. Warning obligations depend on the situation. A warning triangle must give approaching drivers enough warning; the law does not prescribe one universal distance for every road.

If possible, reach the safest available stopping place. Switch on hazard lights, warn other traffic and leave the vehicle and carriageway promptly. Move away from traffic, outside a barrier where one exists. Trafikverket recommends placing the triangle at least 100 m away, preferably farther, and taking care while doing so, walking at the side and outside the barrier where possible. Do not expose yourself in the traffic lane to carry out a roadside repair. Call professional recovery; call 112 when life is in danger.

Use hazard lights, move towards the edge or an emergency bay if possible and switch off the engine. For a non-urgent incident, Trafikverket advises staying in the car or protected from traffic close to it while calling for assistance. In an urgent situation, leave for the nearest emergency exit and use the assistance point, emergency phone or 112. In a fire, leave and reach an emergency exit; follow signs, announcements and emergency personnel. Do not turn a non-urgent-tunnel recommendation into advice to stay beside a fire.
Recognise tunnel safety equipment Independent official examples. The displayed 2.0 km and 100 m belong to these sample signs; they are not universal emergency distances.

On an ordinary road, assess traffic, visibility and the location before choosing a protected waiting place and arranging help. Do not assume that a procedure for a sheltered bay, an exposed motorway shoulder and a smoke-filled tunnel can be identical.
Keep the hot coolant cap closed

children.text: Overheating · Leave the hot cap closed.

text.text: In a conventional pressurised cooling system, hot coolant and steam can remain under pressure even after the engine is switched off. Opening the radiator cap, or the cap of a pressurised coolant reservoir, can release that pressure and expel scalding liquid or steam, causing severe burns. Never loosen or remove the cap while the engine or cooling system is hot. Switching off is not proof that pressure and heat have disappeared.

label.text: Manufacturer handbook: hot coolant and pressure warning

text.text: Treat a temperature warning as a reason to respond according to the actual vehicle handbook, not as an invitation to open a cap. Revisit

for warning indicators and fault recognition. Protect people from traffic first and arrange professional assistance where needed. Cooling-system layouts and stopping instructions vary; this lesson gives no fixed waiting time, cap-opening sequence or roadside refill procedure.

label.text: Trafikverket: protect people and call recovery

text.text: The temperature warning appears on a motorway journey. After reaching the safest available stopping place as conditions allow, follow the vehicle's stopping instructions and this lesson's motorway scene-safety advice. A passenger suggests opening the coolant cap immediately because the engine is now off. Reject that action: residual heat and pressure can still cause a burn. Call recovery from a protected position rather than attempting an exposed repair. If the event is in a tunnel, use the tunnel response above; smoke, fire or danger to life requires the urgent response, not waiting beside the vehicle to diagnose it.

text.text: No. The duty to remain and assist applies regardless of fault.
Identify scene-safety, emergency-contact and first-aid learning needs following a collision.

If involved in a traffic accident, remain at the scene, help injured people to the extent of your ability and assist with necessary measures. Provide your name, address and information when requested by another involved person or someone whose property was damaged. Notify the owner or police promptly if damaged property has nobody present to receive the information. Notify police promptly for a personal injury that is not insignificant.

A vehicle creating danger or obstruction after a collision should be moved to a suitable place. However, where someone has died or been seriously injured, move it only if it endangers other traffic, and preserve evidence as required. Staying at the scene does not mean standing in an active traffic lane. Protect yourself and others while arranging help.

At danger to life, call 112. Give the location, direction of travel, what happened and what dangers you can see; follow the operator's instructions. Make observations from a safe position rather than walking into moving traffic to gather details.
Recognise warnings at an incident Recognition examples only. Neither sign authorises a learner to manage traffic or stand in an active lane.
Use

to learn more about helping someone in an acute situation, including when a person is unconscious or has breathing difficulties. Practical first-aid training can help you prepare. This lesson is deliberately brief and does not reproduce clinical procedures or a pulse-check sequence. In an emergency, call 112 rather than spending time searching a website.

Trafikverket advises calling 112 and marking the collision location safely so responders can find it, even if the animal has left. Avoid approaching an injured animal. Its guidance gives a separate precaution for wild boar, bear, lynx and wolf: continue 200 m before stopping and marking, then call police immediately. Only move the vehicle when safe and possible; explain the actual collision location and the animal's direction clearly. This is agency safety guidance, not a claim that every animal species has identical statutory reporting rules.

caption.text: Call from a protected place, away from traffic. For a life-threatening emergency, call 112 and describe the location, direction of travel, what happened and immediate dangers. Follow the operator's instructions.

text.text: After a collision, a person is badly injured and vehicles are still passing. You call 112 and describe the immediate traffic danger from a protected position, following instructions and helping within your ability. Photographing damage is not the first priority.

This exercise brings the earlier lessons together. It is an original learning scenario, not an official test question or a court case.

You plan to take a passenger to a rural appointment using an unfamiliar car. The outward journey includes a residential area, a roundabout and a faster road. Rain is expected later. At the destination, the nearest empty space is before a pedestrian crossing. On the return journey you become delayed; the passenger asks you to pass a slower vehicle near a bend.
Before leaving, establish fitness, entitlement, vehicle readiness, passenger protection and the controls you may need. Check the route and alternatives.
In the residential area, identify crossings, people hidden by parked vehicles and the applicable speed. At the roundabout, separate entry, lane and exit decisions.
On the faster section, preserve a following gap and a view ahead. If the weather worsens, reassess both lighting and speed.
At the destination, apply the stopping restrictions before considering convenience. Choose a lawful place with a safe manoeuvre and passenger exit.
On the return trip, reject an overtaking attempt without a complete clear path. Change the arrival expectation instead of the safety margin.
The rules behind these decisions are explained in
. The duties to adapt speed, yield where required and avoid dangerous manoeuvres remain applicable throughout.

The official theory test covers vehicle knowledge/manoeuvring, environment, road safety, traffic rules and personal factors. It checks understanding across those areas; memorising the wording of practice questions is not equivalent preparation. The practical test requires you to apply knowledge through vehicle checks, manoeuvres and driving in traffic.

children.text: Current standard theory-test format, checked 1 October 2026:

text.text: 70 questions, of which 65 count towards the score; at least 52 points are needed to pass; standard time is 50 minutes. These administrative figures can change, so verify them before booking. They are not a recommended pass mark for this book's short learning checks.

Trafikverket provides language options, including English, and application routes for support such as extended time, oral support or an interpreter where appropriate. Support generally needs approval before the supported test can be booked. Check the current requirements and apply early enough for a decision; do not assume that support can be added at the door.

Review three kinds of evidence: Can you explain the rule and its exceptions? Can you recognise the situation without a prompt? Can you act safely and consistently during supervised practice? A high confidence rating with little evidence is a learning signal, not a readiness certificate.

Write your next practice plan in concrete terms: “Recognise cycle passages after a turn and explain the duty before reaching them,” or “Demonstrate the safety check and explain each defect response.” Revisit errors after a delay and in a changed scenario so that you are practising understanding rather than recognising an answer.

A learner answers most checks correctly but still needs reminders to scan at junctions. They continue targeted supervised practice instead of treating their theory score as proof of practical readiness.

text.text: Continue your practice record

A useful entry identifies something observable. “Check the near cycle path before the turn, then revisit it as the gap develops” is more actionable than “be better at junctions.” Keep adapting the task to your own experience and the feedback from your instructor or supervisor.
APPENDICES AND SOURCES · 2026 version

Appendix A · Put the learning into practice Appendix B · Learn signs by the decision they require Appendix C · A practical Swedish–English glossary Appendix D · Personal practice record Sources and references Sign groups RB01–RB24 Sign code and family lookup This material is a learning aid to help you understand Swedish driving theory. It is not an official source and cannot replace official information from Trafikverket and Transportstyrelsen. Always consult their current guidance and the applicable rules.

Original source checks are dated 1 October 2026. Chapter additions retain their individual 12–13 October checks below and in the evidence records. Official agency, legal, public-health and research references are distinguished from manufacturer technical handbooks. Use current guidance and the actual vehicle handbook; references do not make this book official. Chapter evidence records exact passages, dates and limitations.

A priority road begins or continues. Still check the actual junction, controls and other road users. Yellow diamond inside a white border.
The priority-road designation ends. Assess the rules at the next junction afresh. Priority-road diamond crossed by a black diagonal band.

This identifies where to stop when a sign or signal requires it. The line alone does not create a universal stop duty. Wide transverse white stop line.

Prepare for a yielding or stopping duty further ahead in your direction. White inverted triangle painted on the road.

and the stop line rather than treating the word as a separate new stopping rule.

Proceed with particular caution and apply the other instructions and traffic rules. Flashing is not demonstrated by the still image. Amber flashing lamp represented by a still drawing.

This identifies a pedestrian crossing. At an uncontrolled crossing, drivers yield to people who have entered or are about to enter. Pedestrian on crossing stripes within a white triangle on blue.

This identifies a cycle crossing. Drivers yield to cyclists and class II moped riders on or about to enter it; riders must also consider approaching vehicles. Cyclist above a crossing in a blue square.
This marks the pedestrian crossing associated with
. Identify whether it is signal-controlled before applying the crossing duties. Parallel white crossing stripes.

and the give-way marking
; assess the controls and your movement. Two parallel rows of white blocks marking the sides of a cycle passage or crossing.

caption.text: This shows a suitable route for pedestrians, cyclists or class II moped riders, according to context. White arrow points right.
This identifies a path or suitable route for bicycles and class II mopeds. White bicycle road marking.
This identifies a path or suitable route for pedestrians. White adult and child road marking.
People with impaired vision commonly use the area. Give them time and space without assuming they have seen you. Five black dots arranged horizontally on yellow.
People with impaired hearing commonly use the area. Do not assume a horn will be heard. Three black dots inside a black circle on yellow.

Skiers often cross or remain on the road here. Watch both sides and adjust speed so that you can respond to a skier entering your path. The skier symbol identifies this hazard; it does not designate a ski facility.

caption.text: Indicates a suitable position for cyclists and class II moped riders. The marking may be adapted to the conditions at the site. The question illustration shows a cycle symbol and an advanced marked area. It does not by itself grant priority over conflicting traffic.

caption.text: This identifies a pedestrian crossing. At an uncontrolled crossing, drivers yield to people who have entered or are about to enter. Mirrored pedestrian on crossing stripes within a white triangle on blue.
Prepare for a roundabout and identify the entry instructions before reaching it. Circulating arrows inside a warning triangle.
Follow the roundabout circulation. Identify the yielding instruction at the entry separately. Three white arrows circulate anticlockwise on blue.
Two lanes or carriageways join. Drivers must adapt with mutual consideration; this is not an instruction to force a gap. Two paths combine into one upward arrow.
The number of lanes increases. Read the diagram for direction and any physical separation. An additional lane opens on the left.
The number of lanes decreases. Use the diagram to plan a safe change early. The left-hand lane merges into the remaining forward lane.
The arrows show the travel direction in each lane; any separation shown is part of the layout. One opposing lane on the left and two forward lanes on the right.

The diagram shows a joining road with an acceleration lane. It does not give a joining driver an unconditional right to enter. A road joins from the right through an acceleration lane alongside one forward lane.
The joining road continues in a separate lane. Read the actual lane layout and markings. A joining road becomes a separate forward lane beside two existing lanes.

sign_entries.english_label: Joining road with its own lane

caption.text: The arrows show the travel direction in each lane; any separation shown is part of the layout. One opposing lane and one forward lane with a divider between them.

Special pedestrian-street rules apply, including walking pace and yielding to pedestrians. Motor access is restricted to the permitted purposes; it is not a general shortcut. Adult and child within a blue rectangular sign.
The pedestrian street ends. Reassess the rules before entering another road. Pedestrian-street symbol crossed by a red diagonal.

Drive at walking pace and yield to pedestrians. Parking is generally prohibited except where a lawful signed arrangement provides otherwise. Street scene with pedestrians, a car, houses and a playing child.
The walking-speed area ends. Leaving it does not give you priority over the road you enter. Walking-speed street scene crossed by a red diagonal.
The maximum is 30 km/h and motor vehicles must adapt to bicycle traffic. Apply the cycle-street entry, exit and parking rules too. Bicycle with a smaller car above it on blue.
The cycle street ends. Apply the yielding rule when leaving it for another road. Cycle-street bicycle and car crossed by a red diagonal.
Parking is prohibited on the signed side for the applicable extent. This does not make stopping lawful where another rule prohibits it. Single red diagonal across a blue circle.
The parking prohibition applies on dates with an odd number. Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Single upright stroke on the no-parking symbol: odd-numbered dates.

sign_entries.official_name_sv: Förbud mot att parkera fordon på dag med udda datum

caption.text: The parking prohibition applies on dates with an even number. Read the time and extent qualifications as well. Two upright strokes on the no-parking symbol: even-numbered dates.

sign_entries.official_name_sv: Förbud mot att parkera fordon på dag med jämnt datum

caption.text: On even dates, do not park on the side with even address numbers; on odd dates, do not park on the odd-numbered side. Check any time conditions. Odd/even-date symbols divided by a red diagonal.
Both stopping and parking are prohibited for the indicated extent. Waiting with the engine running is not a general exemption. Red cross on a blue circle.

caption.text: Read the stated purpose. A loading place concerns loading or unloading heavy or bulky goods, not unrestricted waiting. Lastplats: loading place.

caption.text: The place reserved for the stated purpose ends. Loading-place symbol crossed by black lines.
This space is intended for turning and parking is prohibited. If a no-stopping symbol is inserted, stopping is prohibited too. Vändplats with a no-parking symbol.
The signed turning area ends. Turning-area sign with a no-parking symbol, crossed out.
Read the inserted prohibition and its times together with the sign above. This panel can qualify or vary that sign; artwork variants are not interchangeable. No parking, 8–18.

sign_entries.official_name_sv: Särskilda bestämmelser för stannande och parkering

caption.text: Parking is permitted subject to the sign's extent, panels and other applicable restrictions. The sign does not automatically cancel general stopping and parking prohibitions. White P on blue.
The inserted restrictions or permissions apply throughout the signed area. Locally signed exceptions do not automatically end the wider zone rule. Zone board displaying no parking.
The zone restriction or permission shown by the matching
sign ends. Zone board crossed by black diagonal lines, ending no parking.
This identifies a stop for scheduled services and school transport. Keep the stopping area available and watch for passengers. White bus on a blue rectangular sign.
Read the parking permission, duration and times together with the sign above. The conditions may vary the main restriction. Parking permitted for 30 minutes during 8–18.
Below
, the parking instruction applies to users entitled to park with the specified accessible-parking permit. Read any time limits too. White wheelchair symbol on blue.
Pay according to the stated tariff and follow the other conditions at the payment facility. Read any time qualification. Text Avgift: fee.
Indicate the start of parking with a parking disc or equivalent. Read the applicable time and duration conditions. Parking-disc symbol with 2 tim and 8–17.
This gives the longest permitted parking time. Any time panel determines when the qualification applies. 2 tim: maximum two hours.
Residents with the required permit may park under the stated special conditions. Residence alone is not enough. Text Boende: resident conditions.
Parking is free, but a parking ticket must be used. Do not interpret the ticket symbol as a fee requirement. Text P-biljett: parking ticket.
Park in the arrangement shown by the panel, as adapted to the parking place. Vehicles positioned perpendicular to the panel's lower edge.

or

Enter the inspection site as directed. If vehicle symbols are displayed, the instruction applies to those vehicle groups. Kontroll, goods-vehicle symbol and arrow pointing up-right.

sign_entries.official_name_sv: Följ efter och stanna bakom polisfordonet när detta stannar

sign_entries.official_name_sv: Kör in till vägkanten och stanna framför polisfordonet

Turn sharply in the direction of the yellow arrow or arrows. Temporary use, including roadworks, has a red background. Yellow chevron points left on blue.

The barrier indicates that the road is wholly or partly closed to traffic. Red-and-yellow road barrier.
The crossed-out destination instruction is temporarily not valid. Read the replacement route guidance. Red cross over temporarily cancelled destination information.
This identifies the centre around which vehicles circulate in the roundabout. A horizontal blue board bears successive white arrows pointing right.
This makes the supporting sign or traffic device easier to see. It is not a separate destination or priority instruction. Blue and white bands around a signpost.

Pass on the side towards which the yellow diagonal stripes slope down. A temporary horizontal-striped version permits passage on either side. Two red boards have yellow diagonal bands sloping down towards opposite outer sides.
